A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynamicCity and retain the same core framework. Their main text and Appendices A–E, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite the revised title and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, generation and ablation experiments on CarlaSC and Occ3D datasets, including quantitative tables and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds occupancy forecasting, a user study, computational comparisons and additional generation results.

M1.justification: The core HexPlane VAE, Projection Module, ESS and DiT remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds limited procedural adaptations: masking and shifting latent representations for outpainting, and fine-tuning with first-frame HexPlane conditions for single-frame-conditioned generation.

E1.justification: The datasets are retained, but task coverage expands substantially. Occ3D-nuScenes gains an explicit occupancy-forecasting evaluation beyond reconstruction (B.2), while CarlaSC gains spatial outpainting and single-frame-conditioned generation scenarios (C.7–C.8).

E2.justification: v2 adds actual comparisons with OccWorld-O for forecasting (Table 8) and SemCity for generation (Table 15), substantially broadening the evaluated comparator set beyond OccSora. v1 mentioned SemCity in Table 2's caption but included no SemCity result row.

E3.justification: A.2 revises the stated 2D evaluator setup from pre-trained InceptionV3/VGG-16 to explicitly training both on semantic colormaps. New protocols include forecasting with four context frames covering two seconds and a two-second prediction horizon, a 42-volunteer study rating 20 samples on four five-point scales, and separate VAE/DiT resource comparisons. These changes do not establish that the core generators were retrained.

E4.justification: The original component, downsampling and rollout ablations remain unchanged. v2 adds substantial supplementary assessment of perceived quality and temporal consistency through human ratings (B.3), and systematically examines training/inference time, memory and model-size tradeoffs against OccSora (B.4).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new user study supplies participant/sample counts and aggregate ratings, but introduces no uncertainty reporting or repeated-run estimation practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces its 2D scores alongside the revised evaluator description: DynamicCity's CarlaSC FID changes from 10.95 to 12.94 and Waymo FID from 7.138 to 36.73. These are not established same-setting performance changes; the table's 3D scores and Tables 1 and 3–7 are retained. New Tables 8–15 and Figures 17–18 report forecasting, human ratings, resource costs, SemCity comparisons and additional applications. Findings include higher mean user ratings, mixed efficiency advantages and lower recall than SemCity.

T1.justification: The HexPlane definitions, projection and decoding mathematics, losses, metric formulas, guidance and inpainting equations are substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal derivation accompanies the additional applications.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline reconstruction/efficiency gains remain the same. Replacing 'LiDAR' with '4D occupancy' clarifies the semantic voxel representation already specified in v1; the added appendix evidence does not revise the main contribution claims.

C2.justification: A.3 adds an argument that sparse convolutions offer limited VAE efficiency gains and cannot be applied to its decoder. B.4 acknowledges quality-versus-runtime/memory tradeoffs. The long-sequence caution added in A.5 largely repeats limitations already present in v1's D.3.

D1.justification: v2 reports that code and models have been released, replacing v1's future code-release promise. It also documents the new application procedures, evaluator training data and resource measurements. Existing hardware, optimizer, architecture and training-schedule disclosures remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to OccWorld, CityDreamer4D and Generative Gaussian Splatting for Unbounded 3D City Generation, and removes Xu et al.'s contrastive-superflow reference. It also expands discussion of XCube's sparse architecture, while retaining the overall related-work organization and positioning.

P1.justification: The title and terminology shift toward urban scenes and occupancy, with localized prose edits, acknowledgments and additional appendix subsections. Most existing paragraphs and the main narrative structure remain intact; the scientific additions do not constitute an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a substantial set of displays: forecasting, user-study, resource and SemCity Tables 8–15, a rendering example in Figure 8, and application Figures 17–18. Original Figures 8–15 are retained as Figures 9–16, rather than replaced; the main diagrams and existing table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new forecasting and SemCity comparisons, human ratings and explicit resource measurements strengthen validation beyond v1's predominantly automatic comparisons with OccSora and make practical tradeoffs clearer. However, integration remains incomplete: Table 2 revises 2D scores while Table 5 retains the old scores without explaining different settings, and broad speed/memory superiority claims persist despite mixed resource results. The additions therefore provide a useful but qualified overall improvement.
